memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And if any of the meat of the ordination ram or any bread is left over till morning, burn it up. It must not be eaten, because it is sacred." - Exodus 29:34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Leftovers from the sacred meal were to be burned, not saved for later. Nothing holy was to be treated as ordinary food, casually kept and casually consumed the next day. The instruction guarded against something precious slowly becoming commonplace.

Familiarity is a genuine danger with sacred things. What once moved us can become routine. The believer who wept at the cross years ago can sit through communion thinking about lunch. The Bible that once felt like living water can become a book we skim. Nothing has changed about the holy thing; what has changed is us.

Jesus warned the church at Ephesus that though they had endured and worked hard, they had forsaken the love they had at first (Rev 2:4). Familiarity had dulled them. If you sense that happening — that the gospel has become background noise rather than astonishing news — do not accept it as inevitable. Ask God to restore your sense of wonder. Come back to the cross and look again at what it cost. Sacred things deserve better than our casual handling.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Have sacred things become routine and commonplace to me?
What would help restore my sense of wonder at the gospel?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for handling holy things carelessly and letting wonder fade. Restore my astonishment at the cross, and keep my heart tender toward what is sacred. Amen.
